headline: GOLD ENDS WEEK AT $4,104 AS US-IRAN CEASEFIRE COLLAPSES — OIL +7.1%, SAXO SEES BASE-BUILDING AHEAD OF CPI
snippet: Gold settled at $4,104.10 on COMEX Friday — down 0.21% for the week — after the U.S.-Iran ceasefire memorandum collapsed Thursday, sending Brent crude up 7.1% over five sessions and reigniting inflation concerns ahead of the Federal Reserve's September meeting. Iranian forces struck U.S. military infrastructure in Gulf states following American strikes in Iran's southern provinces, ending a three-week pause. Saxo Bank's Ole Hansen identified the operative dynamic: gold is now travelling through the 'oil → CPI → Fed' transmission channel rather than a direct safe-haven bid, making Monday's July 14 CPI the single most important variable — a sub-3.8% print undercuts the hawkish case and enables gold to recover from this correction, while 4.0%+ confirms September rate-hike odds and extends pressure toward the $3,800 floor HSBC projects as a downside scenario.

headline: GOLD MINERS' NEAR-RECORD Q2: SECTOR UNIT PROFITS EST. $2,787/oz (+50% YoY) — GDX TOP 25 APPROACHING ALL-TIME PEAK EARNINGS
snippet: Adam Hamilton's July 10 GoldSeek analysis documents the extraordinary profit backdrop for gold mining equities heading into Q2 2026 earnings season: assuming gold averaged just above $4,000 through Q2 with stable operating costs, the GDX top-25 producers are tracking toward estimated unit profits of $2,787 per ounce — a 50% year-over-year increase from Q2 2025's $1,861, the second-highest quarterly unit profit in modern mining history behind only Q1 2026's record $3,129. The central paradox: these record fundamentals exist against a backdrop where major miners are trading 15–25% below their January 2026 peaks — Agnico Eagle -15%, Kinross -22%, Alamos Gold -26% — creating the largest P/NAV-vs-gold-price discount since the 2022–2023 bear market trough and, Hamilton argues, a powerful asymmetric setup ahead of Q2 earnings releases over the next three weeks.

headline: TOREX GOLD Q2: 96,297 oz AuEq FROM MEDIA LUNA — GRADE CYCLE ON PLAN, H2 RECOVERY GUIDES 420-470k oz (TSX:TXG)
snippet: Torex Gold Resources (TSX: TXG) reported Q2 2026 production of 96,297 gold equivalent ounces from its Media Luna underground complex in Guerrero, Mexico — tracking to plan as the mine cycles through lower-grade and lower-recovery ore zones deliberately scheduled for H1 2026. Year-to-date production of 197,171 oz AuEq is running at the pace required for full-year guidance of 420,000–470,000 oz AuEq, with CEO Andrew Snowden confirming grades and gold recoveries 'are expected to improve through the second half of the year.' Media Luna entered production in April 2024 after one of the most successful underground construction programs in recent Latin American mining history; its H2 grade recovery trajectory — at $4,000+ gold and with sustaining capex funded from operating cash flow — is the margin expansion story that distinguishes Torex among self-funded mid-tier producers.

headline: K92 MINING Q2 RECORD: 225,965t PROCESSED (+73% YoY), 46,093 oz AuEq — LOWER KORA RAMP ON TRACK (TSX:KNT)
snippet: K92 Mining (TSX: KNT) reported July 8 that its Kainantu Gold Mine in Papua New Guinea's Eastern Highlands processed a record 225,965 tonnes in Q2 2026 — up 73% year-over-year and 59% quarter-on-quarter — at a head grade of 6.7 g/t AuEq, producing 46,093 oz AuEq including 42,931 oz gold, 1.78 million lbs copper, and 50,109 oz silver. Record quarterly lateral development of 3,326 metres and record ore tonnes mined of 228,254 confirm the Lower Kora second mining front, which delivered first stope ore in April, is ramping ahead of plan. K92 reiterates full-year guidance of 190,000–225,000 oz AuEq, weighted to H2 as multiple fronts simultaneously contribute ore. Kainantu's 6.7 g/t run-of-mine head grade generates exceptional per-ounce economics at $4,000+ gold — the 73% throughput increase is the clearest quarterly validation of the expansion thesis that has made K92 one of the TSX's most distinctive high-grade growth stories.

headline: FIRST MAJESTIC RAISES 2026 SILVER GUIDANCE 10% AFTER RECORD SANTA ELENA + LOS GATOS MILL Q2 (NYSE:AG / TSX:FR)
snippet: First Majestic Silver (NYSE: AG, TSX: FR) reported Q2 2026 production of 3.8 million silver ounces and 34,660 gold ounces from four Mexican mines, with both the Santa Elena complex (305,369 tonnes processed, +13% vs. Q2 2025) and Los Gatos mill (record 4,078 tpd average in June) setting record monthly throughputs during the quarter. Simultaneously, the company raised its full-year 2026 silver guidance approximately 10% to 14.6–15.5 million ounces and gold guidance 7% to 128,000–135,000 ounces, with both mill expansions expected to complete during Q3. A simultaneous throughput record and guidance upgrade in the same quarter is among the clearest possible operational signals from a silver producer — and at $59/oz silver, First Majestic's fully funded mill expansion program is generating real operating leverage without dilutive equity financing.

headline: AYA GOLD & SILVER Q2 RECORD: ZGOUNDER 1.49 MOZ Ag (+43% YoY), TOTAL 1.68 MOZ AgEq FROM MOROCCAN MINE (TSX:AYA)
snippet: Aya Gold & Silver (TSX: AYA) reported July 8 that its Zgounder Silver Mine in Morocco's Anti-Atlas Mountains produced a record 1.49 million ounces of silver in Q2 2026 — up 43% year-over-year and 18% quarter-on-quarter — with consolidated production reaching a record 1.68 million silver equivalent ounces, up 61% YoY and 12% QoQ. Zgounder hosts one of the world's highest-grade silver deposits and Aya's expansion from 1,100 to 3,400 tonnes per day, completed in 2024, is now delivering its full throughput potential through back-to-back record quarters. Morocco's stable mining regime and direct Atlantic Ocean access make Aya a distinctive low-jurisdiction-risk silver growth story at a moment when most high-grade silver peers operate in Mexico or Central Asia — a material differentiator for ESG-sensitive institutional capital entering the sector at $59/oz silver.

headline: ZACATECAS SILVER MAPS 2.5KM VEIN AT OSO NEGRO SONORA — PHASE 2 SAMPLES TO LAB AFTER 2,340 g/t Ag PHASE 1 (TSXV:ZAC)
snippet: Zacatecas Silver (TSXV: ZAC, OTCQB: ZCTSF) announced July 9 that Phase Two rock chip sampling and vein mapping has been completed at the Oso Negro epithermal silver-gold project in Sonora, Mexico, with samples dispatched to ALS laboratories for gold, silver, and base metal assay — results expected in coming weeks. Geological mapping in Phase Two extended the Prospecto vein system to over 2.5 kilometres of mapped strike and identified additional extensions at the Tere low-sulphidation epithermal vein system. Phase One results established the anticipation context: 156 samples including up to 14.8 g/t Au and 2,340 g/t Ag, with 39 of 134 vein samples above 1 g/t Au and 35 above 100 g/t Ag — a continuously high-grade epithermal corridor that, if Phase Two assays confirm sufficient width and continuity, could support a first drill program in one of Sonora's most historically productive silver-gold districts.

headline: BRIEN LUNDIN: GOLD/SILVER MINERS OFFER RARE GENERATIONAL BUYING DISCOUNT — STOCKS HAVEN'T CAUGHT UP TO $4,100 GOLD
snippet: Brien Lundin, editor of Gold Newsletter and one of North America's most respected precious metals analysts, argues that the current gold/silver mining equity environment represents a 'rare generational opportunity' — the largest miner-to-gold-price valuation gap since the start of the two previous gold equity bull markets (2001 and 2009). Lundin's structural argument: this bull market was propelled by price-insensitive central bank demand rather than Western institutional momentum, which means the 'equity catch-up trade' that historically closes the miner NAV discount has not yet materialised. When it does — triggered by Western institutional re-allocation, which Lundin expects the July 14 CPI print could catalyse by repricing September rate-hike odds — it typically arrives suddenly and in multiples, compressing the current 20–30% miner-to-gold-NAV discount in weeks rather than months.

headline: THE GOLD FORECAST: IRAN WAR ISN'T THE GOLD STORY YOU THINK — CONFLICT ACTS THROUGH OIL-CPI-FED, NOT A FEAR BID
snippet: The Gold Forecast argues that retail investors are systematically misreading the U.S.-Iran conflict's impact on gold: the expected 'safe-haven spike' has not materialised in this war cycle because gold has been repriced since 2025 primarily as a real-yield and dollar-sensitive instrument rather than a geopolitical fear asset. The actual transmission mechanism: U.S. military escalation → oil prices surge → CPI expectations rise → Fed stays hawkish → real yields elevated → gold faces headwind. This explains why gold declined or traded sideways during most escalation phases rather than rallying as historical precedent would suggest. The actionable implication for mining investors: watch 5-year TIPS yields and September Fed Funds futures probability — not Middle East headlines — as the primary signal for when gold equities are ready to recover from the current correction.

headline: WORLD GOLD COUNCIL MID-YEAR 2026: CENTRAL BANK BUYING STRUCTURAL — $4,000 IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING (CNBC VIDEO)
snippet: The World Gold Council's mid-year 2026 gold outlook, via a CNBC video shared on GoldSeek, characterises current gold market dynamics as structurally distinct from prior precious metals cycles because sovereign central bank purchasing — China, Turkey, India, and numerous emerging market central banks — has replaced Western speculative institutional flows as the primary demand driver. With central banks buying 1,100+ tonnes annually since 2022, the WGC argues that gold's $4,000 level represents a structural floor comparable to the post-2009 $1,000 floor that never meaningfully broke over the following decade — backed by a de-dollarisation demand base that is price-insensitive and persistent, not momentum-driven. For junior mining investors: a structural $4,000 floor means company NAV is being valued against sovereign demand as the backstop, not Western speculative sentiment — a material change in the risk framework.

headline: PRECIOUS METALS WEEK IN REVIEW JULY 10: GOLD -0.21%, SILVER -4.47% — MIDDLE EAST DOMINATES, CPI IN FOCUS
snippet: PMI Cayman's weekly precious metals review for July 10, 2026 documents a volatile week shaped by the U.S.-Iran military re-escalation: gold closed down 0.21% at $4,104.10 while silver declined a more significant 4.47% to $59.57, with the divergence reflecting silver's higher sensitivity to industrial demand expectations and the strengthening dollar. Gold spent much of the week under pressure as oil surged 7.1% (Brent), raising CPI expectations that conflict with the Fed's desire to end its hiking cycle, but recovered Friday on bargain buying and technical support at $4,100. The week's close leaves both metals in a holding pattern ahead of Monday's July 14 CPI print — positioning is compressed, directional conviction is low, and the data will determine whether Q3 2026 becomes a precious metals recovery or an extension of the six-month correction from January's highs.
